ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the image there is an approximately square border, and near each of the four corners inside the border there is an animal head pattern of the same style. The ears of the two heads at the top face upward, and the ears of the two heads at the bottom face downward; the two patterns on the left and the two patterns on the right face each other left-right, and the whole is arranged in a 2×2 layout. Reasoning: A vertical line passing through the center of the square can make the two animal heads on the left and the two animal heads on the right coincide with each other, so there is one vertical axis of symmetry. A horizontal line passing through the center can make the two animal heads above and the two animal heads below coincide with each other, so there is one horizontal axis of symmetry. When reflected across the two diagonal lines, the orientation of the animal heads at the corners and the positions of the ears cannot correspond and coincide, so they are not axes of symmetry. Therefore there are 2 axes of symmetry in total.

raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the image there is an approximately square border, and near each of the four corners inside the border there is an animal head pattern of the same style. The ears of the two heads above face upward, and the ears of the two heads below face downward; the two patterns on the left side and the two patterns on the right side face each other left-right, and overall they are arranged in a 2×2 arrangement.

Reasoning: A vertical line passing through the center of the square can make the two animal heads on the left and the two animal heads on the right overlap with each other, so there is one vertical axis of symmetry. A horizontal line passing through the center can make the two animal heads above and the two animal heads below overlap with each other, so there is one horizontal axis of symmetry. When reflected over the two diagonals, the orientations of the animal heads at the corners and the positions of the ears cannot correspond and overlap, so they are not axes of symmetry. Therefore there are a total of 2 axes of symmetry.
